Write a rating and its assessment to a folder for review

Source: R/export_rating.R
export_rating.Rd

Saves everything a reviewer needs to check a rating without asking its author: the rating itself, its assessment if you give one, plain tables of the same content, and a manifest that lets import_rating() confirm that nothing has changed since.

The folder holds:

  • rating.rds and, if given, assessment.rds. These are the record. import_rating() reads them back exactly.

  • limbs.csv, coefficients.csv, evidence.csv, history.csv, support.csv, lifecycle.csv (only if someone has recorded a lifecycle change with set_lifecycle()) and, with an assessment, assessment_checks.csv. The same content as plain tables, for people, spreadsheets and other software. A column that holds a list (evidence metadata) is left out of the CSV and stays in the .rds. A table that does not apply to this class (a FlodeRatingTable holds no gaugings) is not written, and the README says so.

  • README.txt, which says what the folder is, when and with what version it was made, and the rating's lifecycle.

  • manifest.csv, which lists every other file with its size and MD5 checksum. The checksum detects accidental damage and untracked edits. It is not a defence against someone who edits the manifest as well.

Exporting does not change the rating. In particular it never moves the lifecycle on: a draft is exported as a draft. Approval is a decision for a person.

Usage

export_rating(rating, assessment = NULL, path, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

rating

A FlodeRating, FlodeSegmentedRating or FlodeRatingTable.

assessment

Optional. A FlodeAssessment from assess_rating().

path

Character. The folder to write. Created if absent.

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE (default), a folder that already holds files from an earlier export is left alone and an error is raised. If TRUE, only the files this function writes are replaced; anything else in the folder is left where it is.

Value

Invisibly, a list with path and files, a data.table with one row per file written (file, description, bytes, md5).

See also

import_rating(), assess_rating(), fit_rating().

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage <- seq(0.3, 3, length.out = 25)
gaugings <- data.frame(stage_m = stage,
                       discharge_cms = 3 * stage^1.6 * exp(rnorm(25, sd = 0.03)))
fit <- fit_rating(gaugings, quiet = TRUE)
assessment <- assess_rating(fit, reference_time = as.POSIXct("2025-01-01", tz = "UTC"))

folder <- file.path(tempdir(), "example_rating")
out <- export_rating(fit, assessment, path = folder)
out$files[, c("file", "bytes")]
#>                     file bytes
#>                   <char> <num>
#> 1:            rating.rds 12194
#> 2:        assessment.rds  6931
#> 3:             limbs.csv   100
#> 4:      coefficients.csv   220
#> 5:          evidence.csv  1531
#> 6:           history.csv    89
#> 7:           support.csv   460
#> 8: assessment_checks.csv  6516
#> 9:            README.txt  1549

# Read it back: the rating is the same object.
back <- import_rating(folder)
identical(apply_rating(back$rating, c(1, 2))$discharge,
          apply_rating(fit, c(1, 2))$discharge)
#> [1] TRUE
